methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $200M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Sublime Systems is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Leah Ellis and Yet-Ming Chiang that has raised over $200M to date. The valuation analysis relies on a peer universe of three same-sector, same-to-adjacent-stage private companies (KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, and Amogy at $700M), supplemented by a broader comparable set of eight private and one public firm in the climate technology space.

Two triangulation methods apply to this target. Stage-progression analysis uses the $200M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement, yielding $380M. Peer-median valuation across the three identified comparables produces a median of $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B. These methods reflect meaningful divergence, likely attributable to company-specific technology maturity, unit economics, and market timing within the sector.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $323M to $1.1B, with a median of $690M. Key uncertainties include the wide dispersion in peer valuations (reflecting heterogeneous technology risk profiles in climate tech) and the reliance on total raised as a valuation proxy absent disclosed recent pricing. Stage-progression places Sublime at the lower end of peer comparables, while peer-median anchors to the sector distribution.
